title: ML-Driven Discovery of Metastable States
experiments_summary: The study implements an integrated ML-DFT framework for solid-state nudged elastic band (SSNEB) calculations. Two pre-trained ML model architectures are used as DFT surrogates: EquiformerV2 (eqV2, 153M parameters, pretrained on OMAT dataset) and equivariant Smooth Energy Network (eSEN, 30M parameters, also pretrained on OMAT). The workflow involves three approaches: (1) conventional DFT-only SSNEB using VASP as the reference, (2) ML-only SSNEB using either eqV2 or eSEN, and (3) a hybrid approach where ML models first converge the pathway and DFT (VASP) restarts from the ML-converged images. Convergence criterion is set at total force below 0.01 eV/Å on any atom in any image. The framework is validated on two material systems: (a) the ambient-pressure β-to-γ phase transition in CsPbI3, comparing ML-converged paths and ML+VASP restart paths against a VASP-only ground truth, with structural attributes (octahedral tilting angles, bond lengths) and computational cost examined; and (b) the TiO2-B to anatase phase transition, evaluated using DFT-only SSNEB with climbing-image method, eSEN-only SSNEB, and eSEN followed by VASP restart, with energy barriers and computational cost compared across methods. All ML model predictions use a fixed random seed of 42, and no fine-tuning or transfer learning is applied to the pre-trained models.
